intervals.label: KEK-JAEA cooperative agreement
intervals.quote: April  JAEA and KEK signed a cooperative agreement on the construction, research, and development of J-PARC.

intervals.label: construction
intervals.note: Start is the official history entry for December 2001; the end is taken as the month the main ring reached its initial design energy (December 2008), which the same page records. No source read states a formal end of construction.
intervals.quote: December  Construction of J-PARC facilities started.

intervals.label: operating
intervals.quote: December  Initial target energy (30 GeV) was achieved at MR.

name: J-PARC (Japan Proton Accelerator Research Complex)
notes: The English "What is J-PARC" page (j-parc.jp/en/jparc.html) is older than the current facility pages: it gives the linac as "400 MeV (currently operating at 180 MeV)" and the main ring as "50 GeV (currently 30 GeV)".

operator.note: Both official pages state that J-PARC is jointly operated by JAEA and KEK.
operator.value: Operated jointly by the Japan Atomic Energy Agency (JAEA) and the High Energy Accelerator Research Organization (KEK)

summary.plain: A large proton accelerator laboratory on the Pacific coast of Japan, run jointly by two national research organisations. Its most powerful machine drives a beam of neutrinos across the country to detectors in the mountains of western Japan.
summary.technical: Accelerator complex at Tokai, Ibaraki: a 400 MeV linac, a 3 GeV rapid-cycling synchrotron and a 30 GeV main ring, feeding the Materials and Life Science, Hadron and Neutrino experimental facilities. The neutrino facility drives T2K and will drive Hyper-Kamiokande.
